$comment: Conformance vectors for the component-contract catalog GRAMMAR (contracts/component-catalog/schema.mjs). DS-owned and DS-local: this repo is the single producer, so there is no cross-repo vendoring here. Hand-authored on purpose — generating the vectors from the implementation they check would make them tautological. Every case is spelled out in full rather than patched onto a base entry, so a reader can see exactly what one vector asserts. `expectErrorContains` pins WHICH rule must fire, not merely that something failed. Editing this file requires regenerating component-catalog-conformance.sha256 in the same change. specVersion 2 made `props` a RECURSIVE tree: object nodes carry `properties`, array nodes carry `items`, unions carry an array of type names, and a node cut at MAX_PROP_DEPTH carries `truncated: true`. The v2 cases exercise every arm of that recursion in both verdicts, because a validator that only looks at the first level would pass every v1 vector unchanged.

cases.name: valid-minimal-gap-entry
cases.why: The honest baseline: a presentation-only widget with no VoiceOver label and no consumer render test. Both gaps are written as null, not omitted, and not faked as a pass. `sources` is absent — it is provenance, not contract.

cases.name: valid-fully-populated-entry
cases.why: The other end: a label exists and cites its line, a cross-repo behavioral test is referenced as a STRING, and `sources` records where each axis was read.

cases.name: valid-optional-prop-and-union-type
cases.why: `optional: true` means the prop is absent from the source schema's `required[]`. A union type is an ARRAY of type names — v1 collapsed it to a `"string | null"` string, which no consumer could read without parsing prose.

cases.name: valid-empty-props-object
cases.why: Four widgets in this repo take no props at all (dnd-overlay, focus-overlay, book-modal, coming-soon). An empty `props` object is legal; an empty `states` array is not.

cases.name: valid-nested-object-tree
cases.why: The v2 headline. `props` is a RECURSIVE tree, not a flat map: an `object` node carries `properties`, which is a map of nodes, and each of those may carry its own. This is the shape that makes the props axis carry signal — v1 recorded `{health: {type: object}}` for this widget and stopped, which said nothing a reader could check a consumer against.

cases.name: valid-nullable-object-keeps-its-properties
cases.why: `restingHeartRate?: {value, unit}` reaches the generator as `anyOf: [<object>, null]`, so its type set is `["object", "null"]`. `properties` is legal because the set CONTAINS `object` — requiring the bare string `"object"` would drop the nested shape of every optional object in the repo, which is most of them.

cases.name: valid-nested-array-of-objects
cases.why: The other recursion arm. An `array` node carries ONE `items` node, and that node may itself be an object with properties — `books[].title` is only checkable if the element shape survives into the catalog. `items.optional` is always false: an element is not a member of its parent object's `required[]`, so the field has no meaning for it and is written rather than left to a coin flip.

cases.name: valid-object-node-without-properties
cases.why: `bookMeta` is a `Record<string, BookMeta>`, which reaches the generator as `additionalProperties` and has NO static properties. An object node with no `properties` key is therefore legal and means exactly that. It is not the same fact as `truncated`, which is why the two are spelled differently.

cases.name: valid-truncated-node
cases.why: The MAX_PROP_DEPTH escape hatch, written as data. A self-referential prop type would otherwise walk forever and the gate would never finish. `truncated: true` records that children exist and were NOT walked, so a reader knows the subtree is unrecorded rather than empty.

cases.name: bad-spec-version-zero
cases.why: Case zero of the whole scheme. An entry that does not declare THIS grammar version is not readable by THIS grammar.

cases.name: bad-spec-version-next
cases.why: The half-done bump: someone raised the number in the entries but not in the grammar, or the reverse. Both directions must red.

cases.name: bad-spec-version-stringified
cases.why: `"2"` is not `2`. A JSON round trip through a tool that stringifies numbers must not pass.

cases.name: bad-spec-version-missing
cases.why: Absence is not a pass. A missing version is reported as missing AND as a mismatch.

cases.name: prop-missing-optional-field
cases.why: A prop descriptor without `optional` cannot answer the only question the catalog exists to answer about it.

cases.name: prop-missing-type-field
cases.why: Same rule, other field.

cases.name: prop-type-not-a-string
cases.why: `type` is the collapsed source-schema type as a string, never a nested schema node.

cases.name: prop-type-empty-string
cases.why: An empty type string reads as a known type and is not one.

cases.name: prop-optional-not-a-boolean
cases.why: `"false"` is truthy. A string here would invert the meaning of the field under any naive read.

cases.name: prop-descriptor-unknown-field
cases.why: Strict keys. `nullable` looks meaningful and means nothing to this grammar, so it must be rejected rather than ignored.

cases.name: prop-descriptor-not-an-object
cases.why: The shorthand `"profile": "object"` is a plausible hand-edit and is not the shape.

cases.name: props-is-an-array
cases.why: A props LIST loses the names, which are half the contract.

cases.name: nested-prop-node-not-an-object
cases.why: The recursion must validate to the LEAF, not only at the top. A nested descriptor collapsed to a bare type string is the plausible hand-edit, and v1's validator never looked below the first level.

cases.name: nested-prop-node-missing-optional
cases.why: Every rule that binds a top-level node binds a nested one. The error path names the full route to the offending node, so a deep tree stays actionable.

cases.name: nested-prop-node-unknown-field
cases.why: Strict keys apply at every depth. `enum` is real JSON-schema vocabulary and means nothing to this grammar, so it must be rejected rather than carried along as unchecked payload.

cases.name: nested-items-node-malformed
cases.why: The array arm recurses too. An `items` that is not a node describes no element shape.

cases.name: object-properties-not-a-map
cases.why: A props LIST loses the names at depth exactly as it does at the top. `properties` is a MAP of node, keyed by prop name, at every level.
cases.expectErrorContains: props.profile.properties: expected a map of prop nodes

cases.name: properties-on-a-non-object-node
cases.why: Kind and children must agree. A `string` node with `properties` hanging off it is a shape a reader would take at face value, and no source schema can produce it.
cases.expectErrorContains: props.title: has `properties` but its type is "string" — only an `object` node has properties

cases.name: items-on-a-non-array-node
cases.why: The same coupling on the other arm. An object does not have elements.
cases.expectErrorContains: props.profile: has `items` but its type is "object" — only an `array` node has items

cases.name: truncated-false
cases.why: Same rule as `a11y.voiceOverLabel: false`. Absence is the canonical way to say NOT truncated; a second spelling of one fact is drift waiting to happen, and the generator never emits it.
cases.expectErrorContains: props.profile.truncated: expected true or the field to be absent, got false

cases.name: truncated-node-carrying-children
cases.why: `truncated` records children that were NOT walked. A truncated node that also lists some of them claims both, and a reader cannot tell which part of the subtree is recorded.

cases.name: prop-tree-deeper-than-max-depth
cases.why: The cap is a grammar rule, not only a generator behaviour. Nine levels cannot have been generated — the generator truncates at eight — so a tree this deep was hand-written, and accepting it would let a hand-edit smuggle in a shape no source produces. This is also what keeps the validator's own recursion finite.
cases.expectErrorContains: exceeds the maximum prop depth of 8

cases.name: union-type-array-with-one-member
cases.why: Canonical form. The generator collapses a one-member union to a bare string, so `["string"]` is a second spelling of one type — and two spellings make `properties`/`items` legality depend on which one a writer picked.
cases.expectErrorContains: props.profile.type: expected a non-empty string or an array of two or more unique type names, got ["object"]

cases.name: union-type-array-with-a-duplicate-member
cases.why: The generator deduplicates, so a repeat means the array was assembled by hand or by a merge that did not.
cases.expectErrorContains: props.profile.type: expected a non-empty string or an array of two or more unique type names

cases.name: union-type-array-with-a-non-string-member
cases.why: A nested schema node inside the type array is the v1-to-v2 mistake: `type` names types, it never holds a shape. The shape lives in `properties`/`items`.
cases.expectErrorContains: props.profile.type: expected a non-empty string or an array of two or more unique type names

cases.name: group-not-in-known-set
cases.why: `coffee` is a real fixture directory in this repo but NOT a web widget group, so a catalog entry claiming it means the generator read a directory the schema generator does not know about.
cases.expectErrorContains: group: expected one of github, health, identity, location, other, reading, got "coffee"

cases.name: group-wrong-case
cases.why: The Swift directory is `Identity` and the group is `identity`. Mixing them up must red, not silently resolve.
cases.expectErrorContains: group: expected one of github, health, identity, location, other, reading, got "Identity"

cases.name: group-missing
cases.why: Reported as both missing and out-of-set.

cases.name: widget-not-kebab-case
cases.why: The slug keys the fixture filenames, the snapshot filenames and the schema filename. PascalCase would resolve none of them.
cases.expectErrorContains: widget: expected a non-empty kebab-case string, got "BioTerminal"

cases.name: widget-empty-string
cases.why: An empty slug would resolve to every fixture in the group.
cases.expectErrorContains: widget: expected a non-empty kebab-case string, got ""

cases.name: widget-trailing-hyphen
cases.why: `heart-rate-` is not kebab-case. The regex anchors both ends so a stray separator cannot pass.
cases.expectErrorContains: widget: expected a non-empty kebab-case string, got "heart-rate-"

cases.name: states-empty-array
cases.why: A widget with no states has no renderable surface to hold to a contract. Empty is the drift shape a broken directory read produces, so it must never pass.
cases.expectErrorContains: states: expected at least one state, got an empty array

cases.name: states-not-an-array
cases.why: A comma-joined string is a plausible hand-edit and is not the shape.

cases.name: states-contains-empty-string
cases.why: An empty state name is what a filename-slicing bug emits, and it names nothing.

cases.name: states-duplicate
cases.why: The state set is a UNION of two sources (fixtures and snapshots). A duplicate means the union was not deduplicated, which inflates the apparent coverage.

cases.name: a11y-voice-over-label-false
cases.why: `false` is deliberately NOT accepted. An absent label is unknown-until-audited, which is `null`; `false` would assert a finding this generator never made.
cases.expectErrorContains: a11y.voiceOverLabel: expected true or null, got false

cases.name: a11y-claimed-without-ref
cases.why: A claimed label must cite <file>:<line>. An uncitable claim is the fabricated pass this catalog is built to prevent.

cases.name: a11y-gap-with-a-ref
cases.why: The inverse coupling. A gap cites nothing; a ref beside a null label means the two fields disagree.

cases.name: a11y-is-null
cases.why: The axis is an object with two written fields, never an omitted-by-null block.
cases.expectErrorContains: a11y: expected an object, got null

cases.name: a11y-unknown-field
cases.why: Strict keys. A new a11y axis is a grammar change and a version bump, not a field someone adds to one entry.

cases.name: conformance-behavioral-test-is-false
cases.why: Same rule as the a11y axis: the absence of a consumer render test is `null`, a written gap. A boolean here is an unsourced verdict.
cases.expectErrorContains: conformance.behavioralTest: expected a non-empty string or null, got false

cases.name: conformance-behavioral-test-empty-string
cases.why: An empty ref reads as populated and points nowhere.
cases.expectErrorContains: conformance.behavioralTest: expected a non-empty string or null, got ""

cases.name: conformance-unknown-field
cases.why: Strict keys, and the field name matters: `visualBaseline` would imply a self-blessed screenshot counts as conformance evidence. It does not, and adding the axis is a version bump.

cases.name: conformance-is-a-bare-string
cases.why: Collapsing the axis to a string loses the distinction between a populated ref and a written gap.

cases.name: props-ref-empty-string
cases.why: The two refs are what make an entry auditable against real files. An empty one is unauditable.
cases.expectErrorContains: propsRef: expected a non-empty string, got ""

cases.name: swift-props-ref-missing
cases.why: The Swift half of the cross-platform contract is not optional. A web-only entry silently drops iOS from the catalog.

cases.name: generated-by-missing
cases.why: `generatedBy` is how a reader knows the entry was produced, not typed. An entry without it may be hand-written, which is the anti-pattern.

cases.name: entry-unknown-field
cases.why: Strict keys at the top level too. `notes` is where a hand-written prose claim would land, and prose is not checkable.

cases.name: entry-is-an-array
cases.why: A contract file holds ONE entry. An array is the shape a naive merge of two files produces.

cases.name: entry-is-a-string
cases.why: A double-encoded JSON payload parses to a string, and a validator that coerces would pass it.

cases.name: entry-is-null
cases.why: `JSON.parse("null")` succeeds. A null entry must be a validation failure, not a crash.
cases.expectErrorContains: entry: expected an object, got null

cases.name: sources-value-not-a-string
cases.why: `sources` is optional but not unchecked. A number cannot be resolved to a path anyone can read.

cases.name: sources-empty-array
cases.why: An axis listed with no paths claims provenance it does not have.
cases.expectErrorContains: sources.states: expected at least one path

cases.name: many-violations-are-all-reported
cases.why: The validator returns EVERY violation, not the first. A gate that reports one error per run turns a ten-error entry into ten runs.
